parsedVerdict.reasoning: All seven files serve one concern: application use cases for task management, plus their DTO contracts and response mapping in dtos.ts. Every use case gets persistence through constructor-injected ports from the domain (TaskRepository, ProjectRepository, UserRepository, IdGenerator). No file uses a database, ORM or query client directly. Task-status parsing has one home: the domain's parseTaskStatus, called from both create-task and list-tasks. State changes go through Task methods (assignTo, markDone) instead of being written out in the use cases. The non-empty name check in CreateProjectUseCase and CreateUserUseCase looks the same but checks input for two different entities. The not-found guards are one-line repository lookups that throw, not a business rule copied out. I judged neither to be a copied invariant. A stricter reading could count the identical name check as a duplicated validation, which is why confidence is moderate.
